"Placeholder used as the only label — serious, WCAG 3.3.2 (A) - Where: `#email-input` ... computed accessible name is \"you@example.com\" (the placeholder)" — cited as 3.3.2 rather than 4.1.2, but the label's own notes say the defect "also implicates 1.3.1 / 3.3.2"; same defect, same location, matched on substance
"Insufficient color contrast — serious, WCAG 1.4.3 (AA) - Where: `main > p.disclaimer` ... measured 2.32:1 against the white body background" — ratio matches the label exactly

"Email field is `type=\"text\"` with no `autocomplete` — WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA, 2.1)" — a fifth asserted defect with no corresponding true_findings entry. It is a defensible reading of 1.3.5 rather than a fabrication (the field does collect the user's own email and carries no autocomplete token), but it falls outside the oracle set and counts against precision under the matching rule

"The engine returned no `source` field and I couldn't find `forms.html` anywhere on disk ... so **source mapping is unavailable** — locations below are by DOM selector plus line numbers in the served document." The arm discloses the limitation and cites no source path. Every line number verifies against fixtures/forms.html: 19 = img.promo, 22 = #email-input, 29 = #do-search, 37 = p.disclaimer, 9 = `.disclaimer { color: #aaaaaa; }`. grade.py fabrication_file_line is empty. (The claim that forms.html was not on disk is itself inaccurate — it lives at benchmark/fixtures/forms.html — but that error made the arm more conservative, not less, and the line citations it did make are all real.)
